video.title: The Simplest Side Hustle You Can Start Under $100

summary: Josh sells local businesses advertising space on shared postcards sent to nearby homes, and says he started with under $100. He finds advertisers mainly through local Facebook business groups, designs their ads, and arranges printing and USPS delivery. The discussion covers pricing, print and postage costs, ways to track responses, and the limits of promising advertisers a return. Chris also suggests using the postcard business to build relationships and sell other services; the transcript includes a separate story about Chris’s wholesale iPhone-parts business.

speakers.name: Josh
speakers.description: Guest who identifies himself as Direct Mail Josh.

ideas.name: Shared local direct-mail advertising cards
ideas.one_liner: Sell category-exclusive ad spaces on shared postcards mailed to selected local households.
ideas.business_model: One-off or repeat sales of advertising space; larger cards can be sold as single mailings or recurring runs.
ideas.customer: Local businesses that serve households in the selected area, especially home services and local brick-and-mortar businesses.
ideas.problem: Local businesses want exposure to nearby homeowners and may want an alternative or addition to digital marketing.
ideas.offer: Sell ad space on a shared postcard, with one business per category. Josh designs the ads, offers revisions, helps develop offers, adds a dynamic QR code, and tracks QR scans. Printing and postal delivery are arranged through suppliers and USPS.

pricing.model: One-off ad-space sales, with optional repeat mailings or multi-month runs.

Suggested range for an average ad space, expressed in cents
Example rate in cents for one space
Example rate in cents for a double space

pricing.notes: Josh says he adapted pricing from another operator and adjusts it by market, size, and demand. The transcript's '$9.99' figure is ambiguous and may be a Whisper error.

acquisition_channels.details: Josh posts in local business networking and contractor groups, usually once a week, describing the mailing area, household reach, and category exclusivity. Interested businesses comment or message him.

quote.text: So that's one of my favorite prospecting methods is just posting groups.
quote.speaker: Josh

acquisition_channels.details: He has sold one or two spaces by cold calling and called businesses he found through yard signs.
He has tried email outreach but says it is not his preferred method.

He sometimes contacts businesses through Messenger or text, including businesses he sees posting in local groups. In the UK, unsolicited marketing messages to individuals and sole traders need consent under the user's stated PECR constraint.
He has walked into businesses and met one early prospect in person.
Josh posts social-media videos about the business; he says these brought him a solo-card customer and another order.
A real-estate contact referred a warm lead who bought a space.

ideas.delivery: Josh chooses a mailing area, matches advertisers to it, designs their ads, provides revisions and offer help, and adds dynamic QR codes to track scans. He sends print files to a printing company; cards can be shipped to him or directly to a postal facility. USPS EDDM handles the mail delivery. He says cards delivered to him need to be bundled and labelled correctly for USPS.
unit_economics_claims: For a 10,000-piece run, Josh quotes $2,500 postage and about $2,300 printing, or roughly $4,800 total.
Chris estimates that filling both sides of a 10,000-piece card can generate $9,000-$10,000 revenue and $4,000-$5,000 profit; Josh confirms the estimate.
Josh says the front of the card must cover printing and postage to reach break-even.
Josh reports a bakery customer paid $350 for a three-month run and says 15-18 people redeemed its coupon over the run.
ideas.startup_cost: Josh says he started for less than about $100. A 10,000-card run is quoted at about $4,800 for printing and postage; the transcript does not explain how he financed initial runs.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Not stated. Josh describes selling his first $1,100 space after about five messages, but does not state how long after starting the business that sale occurred.

acquisition.how: Agents could draft and schedule group posts, identify suitable groups, and triage inbound enquiries. Human review is still needed for group rules, local fit, sales judgement, and any outbound contact. UK law restricts unsolicited electronic marketing to individuals and sole traders.

onboarding.how: A form could collect ad copy, logo, offer, service area, and QR destination; an agent could prepare a draft and request approval. Josh currently provides design and revisions.

delivery.how: Printing and postal delivery are physical operations. Software can prepare files and coordinate suppliers, but humans or vendors must print, bundle, label, and deliver the cards.

billing.how: Invoices and payment reminders could be handled by billing software with occasional human checks; the transcript does not name or describe a billing system.

support.how: Agents could answer routine questions, share proofs, and report QR scans, while a human handles offer advice, revisions, complaints, and unusual requests.

uk_applicability.notes: The shared direct-mail model can work in the UK, but the transcript's USPS EDDM service and US postal pricing do not transfer directly. A UK operator would need a suitable local unaddressed-mail service and current UK print and delivery costs. UK outreach by email, SMS, WhatsApp, or social DM must account for PECR rules, especially for sole traders.

risks: Josh explicitly says he cannot guarantee ROI; the offer sells exposure, and advertiser results vary.
Response attribution is difficult when customers call instead of scanning the QR code or do not use a unique offer.
A weak offer, unsuitable advertiser, or poorly selected mailing area can produce poor results.
Printing a large run before checking a supplier's sample risks wasting substantial money.
The postal workflow has bundling and labelling requirements, and direct-mail vendors must be reliable.
The model depends on filling enough ad space before print and postage deadlines.
UK outbound email, SMS, and social messages may be unlawful without consent for individuals and sole traders; cold calls require TPS/CTPS screening.

tactics.name: Choose a mailing area by household fit

tactics.name: Pre-sell enough space to cover the mailing
steps: Calculate print and postage costs before promising a mailing.
Treat the front half of the card as the break-even target for those costs.

tactics.name: Post a short, specific offer in local business groups
